title: Unauthorized access to the Q1 confidential draft

verdict.summary: david_m sent three forum posts carrying parameters the application never accepts (lines 168330-168332); the third was accepted. sarah_j opened the post 1 second before her session made the only admin role update in the log (lines 168335-168336), and 19 minutes later david_m downloaded /finance/reports/q1_draft_CONFIDENTIAL.zip, which he had been denied 77 times (line 168338). That night her account logged in from his workstation, after 10 failed attempts over two nights, and took the file again (lines 168343-168346).
verdict.basis: 14 of 180,800 lines break the one user, one IP binding; the only 400 and the only 500 in the file are david_m's two failed payload attempts; and 2 templates occur exactly once, one of them the single admin role update. Those are counts over the whole file, not scores. The one inference is who wrote post 1042, and F7 carries medium confidence for it.

attacker.summary: Works from 10.0.8.45 and from nowhere else, across all 7 baseline months. He was denied /finance/reports/q1_draft_CONFIDENTIAL.zip 77 times before the download at line 168338 and 3 more times from 2026-03-27, once the access had closed again, 80 in all and never 80 before the download, with 1 success in between.

victim.summary: An authorized reader of /finance/reports/q1_draft_CONFIDENTIAL.zip with 1,528 successes on it. She is the only one of the 10 accounts in the file that ever appears on a second address, and that address is david_m's workstation.

findings.claim: sarah_j's account was used from 10.0.8.45, which is david_m's workstation.
findings.method: Each of the 10 users appears on exactly one source IP across the 7 months before March. These 14 requests are the only lines in 180,800 that break that binding, and every one of them puts sarah_j on david_m's machine. This is arithmetic, not a score.

findings.claim: sarah_j's password was guessed from david_m's workstation in 2 bursts of 4 and 6 attempts, seconds apart, on consecutive nights.
findings.method: A burst is 3 or more consecutive 401s from the same user and IP with gaps under 15 seconds. The file contains exactly 2, both sarah_j from 10.0.8.45. That is the finding: the other 889 failed logins have no burst structure at all. Not one pair of consecutive failures from the same user and IP is closer than 174 seconds, and there is not a single run of two.

findings.claim: david_m sent 3 forum posts carrying parameters the application never otherwise receives: action, payload, script.
findings.method: 9,083 requests hit /intranet/forum/new, of which 9,080 carry only `topic`. These 3 are the only ones with any other key, and /intranet/forum/new is the only path in the file that ever carries a query string at all.

findings.claim: sarah_j's session made the only admin role update and the only avatar request in the entire log, two seconds apart.
findings.method: After ID normalization the file holds 27 request templates. Exactly two occur once: /api/admin/role_update at line 168336; /assets/avatar_{id}.png at line 168337. The next rarest template, /eng/api_docs.html, occurs 1,778 times, so there is no gradient here to argue about.

findings.claim: david_m downloaded /finance/reports/q1_draft_CONFIDENTIAL.zip after being denied it 77 times.
findings.method: For every one of the 1,022 user/path pairs, the first 200 where every earlier attempt was a 403. Two pairs qualify and only this one clears a threshold of 5 prior denials: 77 denials before the success, 80 in total, and 3 more afterwards once the access closed again (first at line 178028). The other flip is sarah_j's first read of the same file on day one of the dataset: one denial followed by 1,528 successes, which is an access grant landing, not a breach.

findings.claim: The only 400 and the only 500 in 180,800 lines are david_m's two failed payload attempts, sent before the third one was accepted.
findings.method: Statuses occurring fewer than 5 times in the whole file. Two qualify, and each occurs exactly once: 500 at line 168330 (/intranet/forum/new?topic=lunch_menu&payload=csrf_test); 400 at line 168331 (/intranet/forum/new?topic=q1_updates&action=csrf_role_update). Everything else in the log is 200, 302, 401, 403. A status code that occurs once in 180,800 lines needs no model to be surprising.

findings.claim: david_m is the likely author of the content in forum post 1042, the post sarah_j opened 1 second before her account performed the admin role update.
findings.method: HEURISTIC, and it is the only claim in this file that is not arithmetic. The logs record requests, never post authorship, and a /intranet/forum/new call never records which object it produced. What the logs do record: of 9,081 accepted forum posts, exactly one is followed within 10 seconds by the same user opening a post: david_m's tampered post at line 168332, then his view of 1042 3 seconds later at line 168333. Object 1042 itself predates the incident: it first appears at line 331 on 2025-08-01 and carries 353 events, so he did not create it. He edits that same object once more at line 168339, 21 minutes after the download. Treat the attribution as an inference from sequence, not as a record.

unknowns.text: How the login as sarah_j eventually succeeded. Ten failures across two nights, then a 200 from the same workstation 24.3 hours later (line 168343). In between, the only 8 requests from that machine belong to david_m. None of the 27 templates in the file is a password reset, a token issue or any other credential endpoint, so the mechanism is not recorded anywhere in this evidence.

What forum post 1042 actually contained. The logs record requests and never bodies, so the payload is inferred from its effect. The object carries 353 events going back to 2025-08-01, and the edit after the download shows only a 302, never what changed.

Who granted and then revoked david_m's access to /finance/reports/q1_draft_CONFIDENTIAL.zip. The order is the evidence, not the total: 77 denials come before the download, the download is line 168338, and 3 further denials follow from line 178028 on 2026-03-27, 80 in all. Those 3 reopened denials are the only trace in the file that the access closed again, and they are what puts this unknown here. The one privileged call in the log returns 85 bytes and names nobody, so neither the grant nor the revocation has an author in this evidence.

dismissed.lead: Employees pulling confidential files outside working hours
dismissed.why: Off-hours access happens here, and outside the incident every instance of it belongs to someone entitled to the file, working from their own machine. Of 6,115 successful confidential reads, 10 fall in the 20:00-06:00 window, 0.16% of them, so the hour is rare rather than routine. Rarity is not what clears the lead though: ownership is. 9 of the 10 are authorized readers on their own baseline machines, and the one that is left is the incident itself (line 168345), which the IP binding already names. 5 of the 9 are strictly after midnight (michael_t at 04:47 on 2025-09-27, line 42768; sarah_j at 03:37 on 2025-10-18, line 58456; sarah_j at 02:19 on 2025-12-05, line 93934; sarah_j at 00:08 on 2026-02-19, line 150515; sarah_j at 00:19 on 2026-03-06, line 162048), and exactly 1 of those touches /finance/reports/q1_draft_CONFIDENTIAL.zip: sarah_j at 00:19 on 2026-03-06 from 10.0.5.12 (line 162048), her own machine and a file she reads 1,528 times in this log. The clock never separates the theft from ordinary work; the source IP does. A 20:00-06:00 rule buys 9 false positives and no new true one.

dismissed.lead: The 899 failed logins in the file
dismissed.why: 889 of them sit outside the two bursts, spread across all 10 users and all 8 months (70 to 102 per user), every one of them a lone mistyped password on /api/auth/login. No two consecutive failures from the same user and IP are closer than 174 seconds. Volume is the baseline; the structure in F2 is the signal.

The access model denies constantly by design: 5,324 denials across 10 users, 15 paths and 181 days, 506 to 545 per user. Nobody is unusual for being denied. Out of 2 denial-to-success flips in the whole file, 1 follows a sustained history of denial, and that one is F5.
